text:
Anton Frondell has spent his first full NHL season as Chicago's shutdown center, a hard job for a 19-year-old on a team still learning to win faceoffs. Now he has a bigger one. Connor Bedard hurt his right shoulder again against Toronto on Nov. 17, his third shoulder injury in less than a year, and The Athletic's Scott Powers reported Frondell replacing him on the top line.

The No. 3 pick in 2025 has 11 points in 22 games. The numbers say the defensive role is drowning him for now: Chicago gets under 36% of the expected goals at five on five with him on, eight points worse than without him. Evolving-Hockey's notes from his short debut last season point the same way: weak teammates, plus a lot of chances against.

There are real tools. His top shot speed sits in the 98th percentile of skaters, and he put 9 shots on Boston on Oct. 31 and scored twice. His shooting is a little under league average, so a few more goals are fair to expect. Watch whether top-line minutes with better wingers lift his share, or whether the Bedard hole simply moves onto his line.
headline: Frondell moves up as Bedard goes down
